A gridded dataset described but not loaded (experimental)

Source: R/proxy.R
SpatProxy-class.Rd

A SpatProxy describes one variable of a netCDF file without reading its values: where the data are, how they are stored, and each axis in a fixed form. In terra, "proxy" means the same thing: a SpatVectorProxy describes vector data on disk. Build one with as_proxy().

Usage

# S4 method for class 'SpatProxy'
crop(x, y, ...)

# S4 method for class 'SpatProxy'
show(object)

Arguments

x

A SpatProxy.

y

For crop(): the area to keep, as a terra::SpatExtent or anything with an extent (terra::SpatRaster, terra::SpatVector, an sf object, or a SpatVector3D such as a buffer from buffer_3d()). The result keeps the cells whose longitude and latitude ranges overlap the area's extent, still without reading values, so as_voxel() then reads only those cells from the file. A polygon is cut to its extent; to keep only the cells inside it, mask the voxel with it afterwards. An area in another CRS is projected first, and on a longitude-latitude grid an extent in the other longitude convention (0 to 360 or -180 to 180) finds its cells too. An area that crosses the edge of the grid's longitudes (the antimeridian on a -180 to 180 grid, or 0 degrees on a 0 to 360 grid) is read from both ends of the grid: the cropped grid runs on across the edge, for example from 179 to 181 degrees, so as_voxel() gives one voxel and mask() with the same shape keeps the right cells. A SpatVector3D across the antimeridian has such an extent (see its ext()). A SpatVector3D with no features has no extent, so crop() stops.

...

Not used.

object

A SpatProxy.

Details

A SpatProxy is the planned core data object of ocean3d (SPEC.md, "Data model"). as_voxel() reads one time step of it into memory as a SpatVoxel, with the proxy's depths, depth edges, CRS and date.

Slots

source

A list with type and where the data are: for "netcdf", path, the full path of the file (a path rather than an open connection, so the object can be saved with base::saveRDS()); for "series", path, the files in time order, and steps, the number of time steps in each; for "voxel", voxel, the SpatVoxel in memory.

variable

A list: name, units, long_name, dims (the variable's dimension names in ncdf4 order), dim_lengths, axis_dims (the dimension of each axis), singleton_dims (other dimensions of length 1) and chunksizes (NULL for unchunked storage).

axes

A list with one element per axis, NULL for an axis the variable doesn't have. lon, lat and depth hold dim, centres and cell edges lower and upper, in storage order, and edges: where the edges come from ("bounds", "inferred", or "none" for a single cell without bounds). depth is in metres positive down and also has storage ("shallow_first" or "deep_first"). time holds dim, cftime (a CFtime object, with the file's bounds attached when it has them) and edges ("bounds" or "none"). A one-step climatology, such as a World Ocean Atlas period, has climatology = TRUE, its units and no cftime.

crs

The coordinate reference system, as text.

Experimental

SpatProxy and as_proxy() are experimental. Their slots and behaviour may change without notice while the core object is built.

See also

as_proxy()
